title: Sell a Vacant House in Hampton Roads, VA | Cash or List
description: Own an empty house in Hampton Roads? How vacancy affects insurance, city registration and carrying costs, and how selling as-is can end them.
h1: Selling a Vacant House in Hampton Roads, VA
lede: An empty house costs money every month and gets riskier the longer it sits. Here is what vacancy does to your insurance and your city obligations, and your options.
tldr: Many homeowners policies limit coverage after 30 to 60 consecutive days of vacancy, and some cities, such as Norfolk, require buildings vacant 12 months or more to be registered every year. Chris Jenkins can buy a vacant house as-is or help you list it.

sections.h2: Why a Vacant House Is Expensive
sections.html:
You still pay taxes, utilities, insurance and upkeep on an empty house, and problems go unnoticed. Many homeowners policies include a vacancy clause that limits or suspends some coverage, typically after 30 to 60 consecutive days. GEICO notes that exact terms vary by policy, so read yours or call your agent.

Policygenius warns that a policy can be canceled if an insurer finds the home was vacant longer than allowed. A vacant home policy usually costs more.

Norfolk requires owners of buildings vacant for a continuous 12 months or more to register them every year, per the city’s Vacant Building Registration form. Other cities have their own code enforcement. Virginia Beach, for example, notifies owners by mail and allows from 24 hours to 30 days to correct violations depending on severity.

A vacant house with overgrown grass, broken windows or a leaking roof is the kind that draws complaints. Ask your city what applies to your address.

• List it. Best price if the house is in decent shape, but you pay to prepare and carry it while you wait.
  • Rent it. Turns the carrying cost into income, but you become a landlord, and some cities inspect rentals.
  • Sell as-is to a direct buyer. No repairs or showings, a closing date you choose, and the carrying costs stop at closing.

See cash offer vs. listing to compare what you would keep.

• Call your insurance agent today about vacancy coverage.
  • Keep the lawn, mail and utilities under control so the house does not draw complaints.
  • Winterize if you are in a cold snap and the house is empty. Freezing pipes are a real risk in an empty house.
  • Gather any code notices, repair bills and the age of the roof and HVAC to give a buyer.

faqs: How long can a house sit empty before insurance is a problem?
Many policies limit coverage after 30 to 60 consecutive days, but it varies by policy. Check yours.
Do I have to register a vacant house in Norfolk?
Norfolk requires registration of buildings vacant for a continuous 12 months or more. Confirm current rules with the city.
Will you buy a vacant house in poor condition?
I look at houses in many conditions. Tell me what you know about the roof, systems, water and structure.
Is it better to rent or sell?
It depends on the house and your appetite for being a landlord. I will give you honest numbers for both.
What if there is damage I do not know the cost of?
Tell me what you see. I will walk the property and tell you how it affects the offer.
What if I owe more than the house is worth?
You would need your lender’s approval for a short sale. Talk to an attorney or housing counselor.
Do I need to clean it out first?
Usually not for a direct sale, but I will say in writing what stays and what goes.
As fast as clear title and your timeline allow. Tell me your date and I will say honestly whether it works.
